subject.title: Agent confabulates completed actions on Telegram surface — same config works reliably on Claude Code/Codex

question: Should this issue stay plugin-only under the closed claim-verification direction, or should OpenClaw core add a narrow exact-turn outbound correlation seam for verifier plugins?
rationale: The user-visible failure is important, but choosing between broad core enforcement and plugin-first policy requires maintainer intent because it affects channel delivery semantics, plugin API surface, and compatibility expectations.

options.title: Plugin Policy Plus Narrow Seam
options.body: Keep verifier behavior outside core, but accept a focused runId/outbound correlation API fix if plugin proof shows current hooks cannot safely gate exact Telegram/source turns.

options.title: Plugin Only
options.body: Treat the broad ClawHub/plugin decision as final and ask affected deployments to implement verification using current sessionKey-based hooks despite the concurrency caveat.

options.title: Core Verifier
options.body: Make OpenClaw own built-in success-claim verification even though this adds policy and upgrade-sensitive runtime surface.

recommendation.title: Plugin Policy Plus Narrow Seam
recommendation.body: Keep verifier behavior outside core, but accept a focused runId/outbound correlation API fix if plugin proof shows current hooks cannot safely gate exact Telegram/source turns.

likelyOwner.reason: He provided the closest explicit product-boundary decision for broad claim verification and is tied to adjacent delivery-policy history.
